plan.rule: No answers here; Check 1 and Check 2 answer them in their reveals.

plan.say_it: At most 22 words: AWS KMS is [an AWS managed service] that lets you [create and control the keys] that encrypt your data; your data is encrypted with data keys. (kms-what-it-is-create-control-keys)
plan.problem_it_solves: **The problem it solves.** At most 18 words: every store needs keys for encryption at rest, and someone must control and audit who uses them.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.plan: Seven subsections in this order, as one causal chain that follows one recording: how it is encrypted (1), whose key it is (2), who may use the key (3), how the key changes over time (4), how use ends (5), how the key reaches a second Region (6), and who runs the hardware (7). Each subsection follows CONVENTIONS-2 U1: problem, numbered trace with bold step names, a truth table when the trace has two or more cases, one 'Why does AWS work this way?' reason, Exam signal, Go deeper or Exam trap or Try it where planned, Say it, then Stop and answer. Time boxes sum to 29 min.

sections.heading: A KMS key protects a data key and the data key encrypts your data

plan.problem: A recording is many megabytes, but the Encrypt operation takes plaintext of up to [4,096 bytes] (kms-encrypt-max-plaintext-4096-bytes). Sending every file to AWS KMS would also load the network.
trace: **Ask for a data key.** The application or AWS service calls GenerateDataKey with a KMS key. The KMS API endpoints [authenticate and authorize the request] before the HSMs do the work (kms-faq-two-tier-endpoints-then-hsms).
**Receive two copies.** AWS KMS returns [a plaintext copy of the data key] and a copy [encrypted under the KMS key] (kms-generatedatakey-returns-plaintext-and-encrypted).

**Encrypt locally.** The data key encrypts the file outside AWS KMS. [Remove it from memory as soon as possible] and [safely store the encrypted data key] with the encrypted data (kms-envelope-store-encrypted-data-key).
**Decrypt later.** Send the encrypted data key to AWS KMS; only principals with permission to decrypt with that KMS key get the plaintext back (kms-faq-exported-data-key-encrypted-under-kms-key).
plan.table: Three keys, three places. Columns: Key | Where it lives | Who keeps it. Rows: KMS key, inside AWS KMS and [never leave the service unencrypted] (kms-keys-never-leave-unencrypted); plaintext data key, in application memory for the encryption only; encrypted data key, stored with the data, because AWS KMS [does not store, manage, or track] data keys (kms-does-not-store-data-keys).
plan.why: Why envelopes? Only the small data key request and delivery [reduces the network load] (kms-envelope-encryption-why), and the KMS key itself stays in HSMs validated at [FIPS 140-3 Security Level 3] (kms-hsm-fips-140-3-level-3).
plan.exam_signal: "encrypt files larger than 4 KB with a KMS key" points to envelope encryption with GenerateDataKey, because Encrypt takes up to [4 KB] (kms-encrypt-max-plaintext-4096-bytes). When an AWS service encrypts for you, the service does the envelope work (kms-faq-where-data-encrypted-three-ways).
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: encryption context. An optional set of non-secret key-value pairs; it is [cryptographically bound to the ciphertext], so [the same encryption context is required] to decrypt (kms-encryption-context-same-to-decrypt). It is [not secret and not encrypted] and [appears in plaintext in AWS CloudTrail Logs] (kms-encryption-context-not-secret-in-cloudtrail). A key policy can [require a particular encryption context] (kms-condition-encryption-context). At most 120 words.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: AWS KMS encrypts a small data key, and the data key encrypts your file. The thing to watch is the encrypted data key: keep it with the file.
plan.stop_and_answer: An application encrypts a file with a data key, stores only the encrypted file and deletes both copies of the data key. A month later it must read the file. Can AWS KMS help? Reveal: No. AWS KMS [does not store, manage, or track] data keys (kms-does-not-store-data-keys), so no copy of the data key exists to decrypt.

sections.xref: 21 S3 (server-side encryption options): one sentence that SSE-KMS is the S3 form of this pattern, with an xref marker; do not teach SSE-S3, SSE-C or Bucket Keys here.

sections.heading: The key type decides who controls the key policy and who sees its use

plan.problem: Every integrated service encrypts with some KMS key. The question is who owns that key: who can change its key policy and who can see each use in CloudTrail.
trace: **Create a table.** Amazon DynamoDB encrypts every table; you choose an AWS owned key (the default), an AWS managed key or a customer managed key, and you [switch between these key types at any time] (kms-dynamodb-always-encrypted-three-key-types).
**AWS owned key.** It is [not in your AWS account] (kms-aws-owned-keys-not-in-account) and its keys [do not provide policy controls or CloudTrail logs] (kms-faq-aws-owned-no-policy-no-logs).

**AWS managed key.** An integrated service creates it in your account, with an alias such as aws/ebs (kms-aws-managed-key-alias-prefix-reserved). You can view it and audit it, but you [cannot change any properties of AWS managed keys] (kms-aws-managed-key-cannot-change).
**Customer managed key.** You create, own and manage it; you have full control of its key policy, rotation and deletion (kms-customer-managed-key-full-control).
plan.table: Truth table, one row per key type. Columns: Key type | Key policy | Use in your CloudTrail | Monthly fee. AWS owned: controlled and viewable only by the service | [Not viewable by the customer] | [No fees] (kms-key-type-key-policy-control, kms-key-type-logging-owned-not-viewable, kms-key-type-row-aws-owned). AWS managed: [Controlled by service; viewable by customer] | logged | [No monthly fee] (kms-key-type-row-aws-managed). Customer managed: [Exclusively controlled by the customer] | logged | [Monthly fee (pro-rated hourly)] (kms-key-type-row-customer-managed).
plan.why: Why three types? Control costs effort. An AWS owned key is a good choice unless you are [required to audit or control the encryption key] (kms-aws-owned-key-good-choice-unless-audit); AWS managed keys are [a legacy key type] (kms-aws-managed-keys-legacy-since-2021).
plan.exam_signal: "audit every use of the key" or "control who can use the key" points to a customer managed key, which gives [the most flexibility, policy control, lifecycle management] (kms-faq-recommend-customer-managed-kms-hsms) and full control of its key policy (kms-customer-managed-key-full-control). Do not link the display that starts 'We recommend' (F2).
plan.figures: kms-before and kms-after (see diagrams), after the truth table and before the Exam signal; the Decision record refers to them. No steps under these two figures.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: pick a customer managed key when you must control or audit the key. The thing to watch is the monthly fee for each key.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team must share an Amazon RDS snapshot with another account. The snapshot is encrypted with the AWS managed key aws/rds. Can the team share it as it is? Reveal: No. You [can't share a snapshot] that is [encrypted using the AWS managed key] (kms-rds-aws-managed-key-snapshot-no-share); its key policy is controlled by the service (kms-key-type-key-policy-control).

sections.heading: IAM policies and other accounts count only when the key policy allows them

plan.problem: Chen's question: an engineer has full S3 permissions. Can the engineer read the bank's recordings? The answer depends on the key, not on S3.
trace: **Ask S3.** The engineer's role calls GetObject, and S3 permission allows it.

**Need the key.** To download an object encrypted with a KMS key, the role also needs [kms:Decrypt permissions for the key]; to upload, [kms:GenerateDataKey permissions on the key] (kms-s3-sse-kms-put-get-permissions).

**Read the key policy.** Every KMS key has [exactly one key policy] (kms-key-policy-primary-exactly-one). No principal, [including the account root user or key creator], has permission unless a key policy, IAM policy or grant allows it (kms-no-principal-has-access-unless-allowed).

**Count IAM only if the key policy allows it.** Without that, [IAM policies that allow permissions have no effect] (kms-iam-policy-allow-needs-key-policy). [The default key policy enables IAM policies] through the account principal (kms-default-key-policy-enables-iam, kms-account-principal-delegates-to-iam).
**Another account needs two allows:** [permission in the key policy] and [an IAM policy in the external user's account] (kms-cross-account-key-policy-and-iam-policy).
plan.table: Truth table for kms:Decrypt. Columns: Case | Key policy | IAM policy of the role | Result. Rows: 1 same account, default key policy (enables IAM), allows kms:Decrypt -> allowed; 2 same account, key policy names only admins and does not enable IAM, allows kms:Decrypt -> no effect, denied; 3 same account, key policy allows the role, silent -> allowed; 4 other account, allows that account, allows kms:Decrypt on the key ARN -> allowed; 5 other account, allows that account, silent -> denied. Facts: kms-iam-policy-allow-needs-key-policy, kms-cross-account-key-policy-and-iam-policy. Use the checks as a checklist: no fact gives an order.
plan.why: Why make the key policy the gate? The key owner decides. A key policy [does not automatically give permission to the account] (kms-key-policy-no-automatic-account-permission), so an S3 administrator does not inherit the bank's key. Key administrators [do not have permissions to use] the key (kms-key-administrators-cannot-use-key), and AWS recommends [separating the permissions for key users] and administrators (kms-separate-key-users-and-admins).
plan.exam_signal: "users with full S3 access must not read the files" points to the key policy of a customer managed key: S3 permission without kms:Decrypt does not download the object (kms-s3-sse-kms-put-get-permissions). "Separate the people who manage the key from the people who use it" points to key administrators and key users in the key policy (kms-key-administrators-cannot-use-key).
plan.spot_the_bug: A key policy gives the pipeline role kms:Encrypt and kms:Decrypt on alias/ostell-audio. The role writes new recordings to the ostell/ prefix with SSE-KMS, and the uploads fail. Find the bug. Reveal: an upload needs [kms:GenerateDataKey permissions on the key] (kms-s3-sse-kms-put-get-permissions); kms:Encrypt is not the operation that S3 uses. Story-neutral wording ('A team') is also fine; do not add a story fact.
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: grants and condition keys. A grant allows one principal to use [exactly one KMS key], can allow [but not deny access], and [Grants are often used for temporary permissions] (kms-grant-allow-only-one-key-temporary; write the display in lowercase mid-sentence); AWS services create a grant and retire it [as soon as its task is complete] (kms-grants-used-by-integrated-services); for a new grant [it can take several minutes] to propagate, so a grant token covers the gap (kms-grant-eventual-consistency-token). kms:ViaService limits a key to [requests from specified AWS services] (kms-condition-viaservice). Across accounts, permissions are [effective only for the following operations] (kms-cross-account-only-some-operations), and the calling account pays (kms-pricing-cross-account-caller-pays). At most 150 words.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: S3 permission is not enough; the key policy must also let you decrypt. The thing to watch is the default key policy.
plan.stop_and_answer: A role in account B calls Decrypt on a key in account A. The key policy in account A allows account B. The role's IAM policy in account B has no KMS statement. Does the call succeed? Reveal: No. Cross-account use needs [permission in the key policy] and [an IAM policy in the external user's account] (kms-cross-account-key-policy-and-iam-policy).

sections.xref: 03 IAM (policy evaluation and the IAM-side KMS subsection a-kms-key-policy-decides-whether-iam-policies-count-for-the-key): xref marker in the trace; do not repeat the general IAM evaluation.

sections.heading: Automatic rotation changes only the key material and keeps the same KMS key

plan.problem: The bank's questionnaire asks for yearly key rotation. Callvale fears that it must re-encrypt many terabytes of recordings each year.
trace: **Turn it on.** By default, [key rotation is disabled for customer managed keys] until you enable it (kms-rotation-disabled-by-default-cmk).
**Choose the period.** Without a period, AWS KMS uses [365 days] (kms-rotation-default-period-365-days); a custom period is [between 90 and 2560 days] (kms-rotation-period-range-90-2560-days).

**New material encrypts.** After a rotation, new requests use the newest material, and AWS KMS [keeps previous versions of keys] to decrypt older data (kms-faq-auto-rotation-no-reencrypt, kms-rotation-retains-old-material).
**Nothing else changes.** Rotation [changes only the current key material]; the key stays [the same logical resource] (kms-rotation-same-logical-key-transparent).
plan.table: Rotation by key kind. Columns: Key | Automatic rotation | What you do. Customer managed symmetric key: [Automatic rotation is optional] | turn it on (kms-rotation-only-customer-managed-symmetric). AWS managed key: every year, you cannot change it (kms-aws-managed-keys-rotate-every-year). Asymmetric, HMAC or custom key store key: [not eligible for automatic or on-demand key rotation] | create a new key and move the alias (kms-rotation-not-for-asymmetric-hmac-custom-store, kms-manual-rotation-new-key-alias).
plan.why: Why keep the old material? Rotation [has no effect on the data] that the key protects (kms-rotation-no-reencrypt-of-data); old ciphertext still needs its material. AWS best practice rotates only when you are [required to rotate keys for regulatory compliance] (kms-rotation-best-practice-only-if-required).
plan.exam_signal: "rotate the key every year with the LEAST operational overhead" points to automatic rotation of a customer managed symmetric key (kms-rotation-only-customer-managed-symmetric). "An asymmetric key must be rotated" points to a new key and an alias (kms-manual-rotation-new-key-alias).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: turn on automatic rotation; the key ID and old data stay as they are. The thing to watch is asymmetric keys.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team rotates an asymmetric signing key by hand: it creates a new KMS key. Its applications call the old key by key ID. Do the applications start to use the new key? Reveal: No. Manual rotation means you must [update references to the KMS key ID] or point an alias at the new key (kms-manual-rotation-new-key-alias).

sections.xref: 07 Secrets and certificates owns secret rotation and certificate renewal (bullet 1.3.S7); one xref marker after the table.

sections.heading: A disabled KMS key can be re-enabled but a deleted one cannot be recovered

plan.problem: The bank's contract says access must end quickly when the contract ends. A mistake must still be reversible, because a deleted key loses data.
trace: **Disable.** A disabled key works in no cryptographic operation [until you re-enable it] (kms-disabled-key-no-crypto-until-reenabled). For new requests [the effect is almost immediate] (kms-unusable-key-data-keys-delayed-effect).

**Watch the data keys.** Data keys that are already decrypted keep working until the KMS key is needed again; an attached EBS volume keeps working, and the next attachment fails (kms-unusable-key-data-keys-delayed-effect, kms-unusable-key-ebs-attach-fails).

**Schedule deletion.** AWS KMS requires a waiting period of [7 – 30 days], default [30 days] (kms-deletion-waiting-period-7-to-30-days). In that state the key [cannot be used in any cryptographic operations], and you can [cancel key deletion before the waiting period ends] (kms-pending-deletion-no-crypto-cancel-possible).
**Deleted.** The key material is gone, and for data encrypted under it, [that data becomes unrecoverable] (kms-deletion-irreversible-data-unrecoverable).
plan.table: Key states. Columns: State | Encrypt and decrypt | Way back | Charged. Enabled | yes | not needed | yes. Disabled | no | re-enable | [Disabled keys continue to incur storage charges] (kms-disabled-keys-still-charged). Pending deletion | no | cancel before the period ends | not charged (kms-pricing-no-charge-scheduled-deletion). Deleted | no | none (kms-disable-instead-of-delete).
plan.why: Why a waiting period? Deletion is [destructive and potentially dangerous] (kms-deletion-irreversible-data-unrecoverable), so AWS KMS gives you time to find data that still needs the key. AWS suggests [disabling the KMS key instead of deleting it] when you are not sure (kms-disable-instead-of-delete).
plan.exam_signal: "stop all use of the key as soon as possible, but keep the option to restore access" points to disabling the key (kms-disabled-key-no-crypto-until-reenabled). "delete the key immediately" is not possible: deletion waits [7 – 30 days] (kms-deletion-waiting-period-7-to-30-days).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: disable the key to stop its use now. The thing to watch is deletion, because it cannot be undone.
plan.stop_and_answer: An engineer schedules a key for deletion with a 7-day waiting period. Three days later the team finds archive files that still need the key. Can the team keep the key? Reveal: Yes. The team can [cancel key deletion before the waiting period ends] (kms-pending-deletion-no-crypto-cancel-possible).

sections.heading: A KMS key stays in its Region unless you create a multi-Region key

plan.problem: At stage 4 the bank needs a copy of the data in a second Region. An encrypted copy is useless there if no key in that Region can decrypt it.
trace: **One Region.** A single-Region key is [stored and used only in the Region] [in which it was created] (kms-single-region-key-stays-in-region).
**Copy with a destination key.** To copy an encrypted RDS snapshot to another Region you specify [the KMS key in the destination AWS Region] (kms-cross-region-snapshot-copy-destination-key).

**Or create a multi-Region key.** Related multi-Region keys have [the same key material and key ID], so data decrypts in the other Region [without re-encrypting or making a cross-Region call] (kms-mrk-same-material-no-cross-region-call).

**Manage each copy.** Each related key has its own key policy, grants, aliases and state: [manage each multi-Region key independently] (kms-mrk-independent-policies-grants-aliases). Rotation is set [only on the primary key] and the new material is copied to the replicas (kms-mrk-rotation-on-primary-only).
plan.table: Columns: Question | Single-Region key | Multi-Region key. Decrypt in another Region? no, re-encrypt with a destination key | yes, with the related replica. Created automatically? n/a | [Multi-Region keys are not global.] (kms-mrk-not-global-never-auto-replicated). Convert later? [You cannot convert a single-Region key] (kms-mrk-cannot-convert). Fee | [$1/month] for each primary and each replica (kms-price-key-storage-per-month).
plan.why: Why are keys Regional by default? Regional isolation: AWS advises a multi-Region key [only when you need one] (kms-mrk-use-only-when-needed), and multi-Region keys make [compliance with data residency mandates] harder (kms-mrk-data-residency-harder).
plan.exam_signal: "decrypt the data in the recovery Region during a Regional outage without re-encrypting" points to a multi-Region key (kms-mrk-use-cases, kms-mrk-same-material-no-cross-region-call). Note in the same callout or the body: S3 Cross-Region Replication still [decrypts and re-encrypts the data keys] under the destination key (kms-mrk-s3-crr-reencrypts).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: a key works in one Region unless you create it as multi-Region. The thing to watch is that each replica has its own key policy.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team wants its existing single-Region key to become a multi-Region key so that its replica can decrypt old data. Can it change the key? Reveal: No. [You cannot convert a single-Region key]; the team must re-encrypt the data under a new multi-Region key (kms-mrk-cannot-convert).

sections.xref: 40 (multi-Region disaster recovery) uses multi-Region keys at stage 4; xref marker in the problem paragraph.

sections.heading: AWS CloudHSM gives you single-tenant hardware security modules that you operate

plan.problem: Some rules require keys in a single-tenant hardware security module (HSM) that only the company controls. AWS KMS is a shared managed service, so it cannot meet that rule on its own.
trace: **Create a cluster in your VPC.** AWS CloudHSM [must be provisioned inside an Amazon VPC] (cloudhsm-faq-requires-vpc); each HSM appears in your subnet through [an elastic network interface (ENI)] (cloudhsm-eni-in-your-subnet).
**Sign in as an HSM user.** Inside the cluster [you use HSM users directly on HSMs], not IAM (cloudhsm-hsm-users-not-iam). AWS [has no way to recover your keys] (cloudhsm-aws-cannot-recover-keys).
**Add a second HSM.** High availability needs [at least two HSMs] in two Availability Zones (cloudhsm-faq-ha-automatic-two-azs).

**Call standard APIs.** Applications use [PKCS#11], [Java JCE] or [Microsoft KSP/CNG] (cloudhsm-faq-standard-apis); AWS KMS offers [no native integration] with them (kms-faq-no-native-openssl-jce-cng).
**Connect AWS services through AWS KMS.** S3, EBS and RDS use CloudHSM keys only [through the KMS custom key store feature] (cloudhsm-aws-services-via-kms-custom-key-store).
plan.table: Columns: Question | AWS KMS | AWS CloudHSM. Who runs the HSMs: AWS | you, with [you have more responsibility] (cloudhsm-more-responsibility-than-managed). Tenancy: shared service | [single-tenant access to the HSM] (cloudhsm-single-tenant-access). FIPS validation: [FIPS 140-3 Security Level 3] (kms-hsm-fips-140-3-level-3) | [FIPS 140-3 Level 3] on hsm2m.medium (cloudhsm-hsm2m-fips-140-3-level-3). Price: per key and request | [an hourly fee for each HSM] (cloudhsm-price-hourly-per-hsm-no-upfront).
plan.why: Why not CloudHSM by default? AWS suggests AWS KMS if you do not want to [operate your own HSMs] (cloudhsm-consider-kms-if-no-hsm-ops), and recommends customer managed keys [created and stored in the KMS HSMs] for [higher performance, lower latency] (kms-recommend-cmk-in-kms-hsms).
plan.exam_signal: "single-tenant HSM", "exclusive control", "PKCS #11" or "SSL offload" points to AWS CloudHSM (cloudhsm-vs-kms-faq-single-tenant-vpc-exclusive, cloudhsm-use-cases). "FIPS 140-3 Level 3" alone does not: AWS KMS keys are protected by HSMs validated at [FIPS 140-3 Security Level 3] (kms-hsm-fips-140-3-level-3).
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: custom key stores. Besides the standard key store, AWS KMS supports two custom key store types: a CloudHSM key store backed by a [dedicated, customer-owned AWS CloudHSM cluster] and an external key store [outside the AWS Cloud] (kms-custom-key-store-two-types). A CloudHSM key store needs [at least two active HSMs] [in different Availability Zones] (kms-cloudhsm-key-store-two-hsms-two-azs), runs at [lower than for keys stored in the default] key store (kms-faq-cloudhsm-ks-lower-request-rate), and has no import and no automatic rotation (kms-faq-cloudhsm-ks-no-import-no-auto-rotation). [External key stores are not recommended.] (kms-external-key-store-not-recommended). Use the exact displays of the fact cards; at most 150 words.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: choose CloudHSM only for single-tenant HSMs that you must control. The thing to watch is the work: you run the cluster.
plan.stop_and_answer: A company must encrypt Amazon S3 objects with server-side encryption, and the keys must be generated and stored in its own CloudHSM cluster. What connects the two? Reveal: an AWS KMS custom key store backed by the cluster; AWS services reach CloudHSM [through the KMS custom key store feature] (cloudhsm-aws-services-via-kms-custom-key-store).

traps.belief: A principal with full Amazon S3 permissions can download every object in the bucket, also objects encrypted with a KMS key.
traps.truth: Downloading an object encrypted with a KMS key also needs kms:Decrypt on that key, and no principal can use a key unless a key policy, IAM policy or grant allows it.

traps.belief: After a key rotation, old data can no longer be decrypted, so you must re-encrypt it or change the key ID in your applications.
traps.truth: Automatic rotation keeps earlier key material to decrypt old data and keeps the same KMS key; you do not re-encrypt your data.

traps.belief: A requirement for FIPS 140 Level 3 validated HSMs needs AWS CloudHSM, because AWS KMS is only Level 2.
traps.truth: AWS KMS keys are protected by HSMs validated under FIPS 140-3 Security Level 3; CloudHSM is for single-tenant HSMs under your exclusive control or for standard APIs such as PKCS #11.

traps.belief: You can edit the key policy or the rotation of an AWS managed key such as aws/s3, or use it to share encrypted data with another account.
traps.truth: You cannot change any property of an AWS managed key, the service controls its key policy, and a snapshot encrypted with it cannot be shared.

traps.belief: An IAM policy that allows kms:Decrypt is enough to use any KMS key of the account.
traps.truth: IAM allow statements have no effect unless the key policy allows IAM policies to control access; the default key policy does, a custom key policy may not.

traps.belief: You can delete a KMS key at once, and data encrypted under it can still be recovered later.
traps.truth: Deletion waits 7 to 30 days, and after deletion the data encrypted under the key becomes unrecoverable; disable the key when you are not sure.

traps.belief: A KMS key works in every Region, or an existing key can later become a multi-Region key.
traps.truth: A single-Region key is stored and used only in its Region, a cross-Region copy needs a key in the destination Region, and a key cannot be converted to a multi-Region key.

traps_from_other_chapters.rule: Distractors may also carry trap ids that other chapters define (lint.traps() knows every brief and hand file). Use these when the wrong belief is an IAM belief, not a KMS one.

story.trigger: The bank's questionnaire asks who controls the keys for the bank's recordings, and how Callvale proves each use of a key.
story.problem: Callvale encrypts its buckets and its database with keys that AWS manages. The bank requires that Callvale controls who can use the key for the bank's recordings. Every use of the key must be logged. Access must end quickly when the contract ends.
story.state_at_month_18: Buckets callvale-audio (with the bank prefix ostell/) and callvale-transcripts; Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (Aurora arrives in chapter 27 at month 20, so it is not in this chapter's pictures); DynamoDB table jobs. Key aliases from STARTUP.md: alias/callvale-audio, alias/callvale-db, alias/ostell-audio.

question.text: If an engineer has full S3 permissions, can that engineer still read the bank's recordings?

story.rules: Question stems never name Callvale or the cast. The story never teaches a fact: a story sentence states no AWS limit, default or can-or-cannot rule. Multi-Region keys are stage 4 (chapter 40): the multi-Region subsection says 'At stage 4' or uses 'A team', and adds no Region pair beyond US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon). CloudHSM is 'weighed, not chosen' (STARTUP A8).

decision_record.context: At most 60 words: stage 3, month 18; the bank's questionnaire; today every store uses keys that AWS manages; the bank wants Callvale to control who uses the key for its recordings, log every use and end access quickly when the contract ends.
decision_record.requirement: Callvale must control who can use the key for the bank's recordings, log every use of the key and end access quickly, with the LEAST operational overhead.
options: keep the keys that AWS manages
customer managed keys in AWS KMS, with one dedicated key for the bank's recordings (chosen)

reasons_with_facts.against_aws_managed: you [cannot change any properties of AWS managed keys] (kms-aws-managed-key-cannot-change)
reasons_with_facts.for_customer_managed: [You have full control over these KMS keys] (kms-customer-managed-key-full-control); each use is logged in CloudTrail (kms-key-type-logging-owned-not-viewable, kms-cloudtrail-logs-all-calls); access ends when the key is disabled (kms-faq-disable-keys-temporarily)
reasons_with_facts.against_cloudhsm: [you have more responsibility] (cloudhsm-more-responsibility-than-managed); AWS suggests a custom key store only when regulations [mandate key material protection in a single-tenant HSM] (kms-custom-key-store-only-if-mandated), and the bank does not

decision_record.decision: Customer managed keys in AWS KMS: alias/callvale-audio, alias/callvale-db and alias/ostell-audio for the bank's recordings.
decision_record.tradeoff: A wrong key policy can stop the pipeline, because no principal can use a key that no policy allows (kms-no-principal-has-access-unless-allowed). Key requests add a cost that grows with volume (kms-faq-billing-keys-and-requests).

question_slots.twin: strict twin pair A, first question
question_slots.plan: A company keeps sensitive files in an S3 bucket that uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed key; the key policy lets IAM policies control access (state this side). A role has s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on the bucket and no KMS permission. Uploads are single PUT requests of small files. The role cannot download objects. Ask: which change gives the role access with LEAST privilege? Shared options for the twin: allow kms:Decrypt on the key ARN; allow kms:GenerateDataKey on the key ARN; allow kms:* on every key (works, violates the qualifier); add s3:* on the bucket (keyword-bait, trap kms-trap-s3-permission-reads-encrypted). Key: kms:Decrypt. Facts: kms-s3-sse-kms-put-get-permissions, kms-iam-least-privilege-key-arns.

An application must encrypt large video files at rest with a KMS key before it stores them. Key: call GenerateDataKey, encrypt the file with the plaintext data key, store the encrypted data key with the file. Distractors: call Encrypt on each whole file (impossible-feature, 4 KB, kms-encrypt-max-plaintext-4096-bytes); export the KMS key to the application (impossible-feature allowed once only: use a misconception sentence for one of the two, kms-keys-never-leave-unencrypted); store the plaintext data key next to the file (wrong-configuration, kms-envelope-store-encrypted-data-key). Qualifier none (difficulty 1). Facts: kms-generatedatakey-returns-plaintext-and-encrypted, kms-envelope-store-encrypted-data-key.

A DynamoDB table uses the default encryption. A new rule says the company must control who can use the key and audit each use of the key in CloudTrail. Key: switch the table to a customer managed key with a key policy (kms-dynamodb-always-encrypted-three-key-types, kms-customer-managed-key-full-control). Distractors: switch to the AWS managed key and edit its key policy (trap kms-trap-aws-managed-key-controllable); keep the AWS owned key and create a CloudTrail trail (misconception: owned-key use is not viewable, kms-key-type-logging-owned-not-viewable); move the key to a CloudHSM cluster (violates-qualifier, trap kms-trap-fips-needs-cloudhsm).

question_slots.worked: the chapter's one think-aloud (six steps, no wrong path)
question_slots.plan: A company encrypts many terabytes in S3 with a symmetric customer managed key whose key policy it must keep. A policy mandates new key material every year. Key: enable automatic key rotation on the key (kms-rotation-only-customer-managed-symmetric, kms-rotation-default-period-365-days, kms-faq-auto-rotation-no-reencrypt). Distractors: create a new key each year and re-encrypt all objects (works, violates-qualifier, trap); a scheduled function that re-encrypts objects under new material (trap kms-trap-rotation-reencrypts-data); switch to the AWS managed key, which rotates every year (different-problem: the company would lose control of the key policy, kms-aws-managed-key-cannot-change). Do not let the 2022 change of the AWS managed period decide the key.

Account A owns a customer managed key; an application role in account B must decrypt data encrypted under it. Which combination of steps meets the requirements with least privilege (Select TWO)? Keys: add a key policy statement in account A that allows account B (or the role) kms:Decrypt; add an IAM policy in account B that allows kms:Decrypt on the key ARN (kms-cross-account-key-policy-and-iam-policy). Distractors: give the role kms:Decrypt on Resource * only (trap kms-trap-iam-policy-alone-opens-key); attach a resource control policy that allows kms:Decrypt (RCPs grant no permissions, kms-rcp-customer-managed-keys-guardrail, trap iam-trap-scp-grants); share the AWS managed key with account B (trap kms-trap-aws-managed-key-controllable).

question_slots.twin: strict twin of the first slot: the stem is identical except 'cannot download objects' becomes 'cannot upload new objects'; the four option texts are identical; the key moves to kms:GenerateDataKey. Place it at least 3 questions after its twin (here it is the sixth slot).
question_slots.plan: Same scenario and options as the first slot. Key: allow kms:GenerateDataKey on the key ARN (kms-s3-sse-kms-put-get-permissions).

question_slots.twin: twin pair B, first question (not strict)
question_slots.plan: Regulations mandate that the keys of a Java application be generated and stored in single-tenant HSMs under the company's exclusive control, and the application calls a PKCS #11 or JCE library. Key: an AWS CloudHSM cluster with HSMs in two Availability Zones (cloudhsm-vs-kms-faq-single-tenant-vpc-exclusive, cloudhsm-faq-standard-apis, cloudhsm-faq-ha-automatic-two-azs). Distractors: AWS KMS customer managed key in the default key store (sibling-confusion: not single-tenant); AWS managed key (trap kms-trap-aws-managed-key-controllable); a CloudHSM cluster with one HSM (wrong-configuration, cloudhsm-single-hsm-can-lose-keys). Options in neutral words so that the twin can reuse them.

An application encrypts data with a KMS key in one Region and replicates the encrypted data to a recovery Region. During a Regional outage the recovery Region must decrypt the data without a call to the first Region. Which combination of steps (Select TWO)? Keys: create a multi-Region primary key and a replica key in the recovery Region (kms-mrk-same-material-no-cross-region-call); write a key policy for the replica that allows the recovery application role (kms-mrk-independent-policies-grants-aliases). Distractors: convert the existing key to multi-Region (impossible-feature, kms-mrk-cannot-convert, trap); use the first Region's key ARN from the recovery Region (trap kms-trap-key-is-global); rely on the replica to copy the primary's key policy (wrong-configuration, kms-mrk-independent-policies-grants-aliases).

A customer contract ends. The company must stop all cryptographic use of that customer's customer managed key as soon as possible, but must be able to restore access if a legal review in 60 days requires it. Key: disable the key (kms-disabled-key-no-crypto-until-reenabled, kms-disable-instead-of-delete). Distractors: delete the key immediately (impossible-feature, trap kms-trap-delete-key-immediately, kms-deletion-waiting-period-7-to-30-days); schedule deletion with the longest waiting period (wrong: the period is shorter than 60 days and deletion is irreversible); remove kms:Decrypt from the IAM policies only (misconception: the key policy can still allow principals directly, trap kms-trap-iam-policy-alone-opens-key). The stem number 60 days is scenario text, not a fact.

A company signs documents with an asymmetric RSA KMS key that its applications call through an alias. A policy says the key must be rotated. What should the company do? Key: create a new asymmetric KMS key and point the alias at it (kms-faq-asym-hmac-no-auto-rotation-alias, kms-manual-rotation-new-key-alias). Distractors: enable automatic key rotation (impossible-feature, kms-rotation-not-for-asymmetric-hmac-custom-store); start an on-demand rotation (misconception: on-demand rotation is for symmetric keys, kms-on-demand-rotation-imported-symmetric); re-import new key material into the same key (misconception, kms-imported-asym-hmac-same-material-only). Qualifier none (difficulty 1).

question_slots.twin: twin of the seventh slot (pair B): the mandate becomes 'keys protected by HSMs validated at FIPS 140-3 Level 3' and the application uses the AWS SDK; the same four options; the key moves to the AWS KMS customer managed key. At least 3 questions between the two.
question_slots.plan: Key: AWS KMS customer managed key (kms-hsm-fips-140-3-level-3, kms-recommend-cmk-in-kms-hsms). The CloudHSM option works but violates the qualifier (trap kms-trap-fips-needs-cloudhsm). The FIPS change of 2023-05-24 is outside the 24-month volatile window; still let the explanation rest on kms-hsm-fips-140-3-level-3, not on the change fact.

A security team created a key with a custom key policy that names only its own administrator role. Developer roles have IAM policies that allow kms:Decrypt on the key ARN, but their calls fail. The team wants to centrally manage access to this key with IAM policies from now on. Key: add the key policy statement that allows the account principal, which enables IAM policies (kms-default-key-policy-enables-iam, kms-account-principal-delegates-to-iam, kms-iam-policy-allow-needs-key-policy). Distractors: give the developer roles kms:* on Resource * (trap kms-trap-iam-policy-alone-opens-key); create a grant for each developer role (works for now, violates the qualifier, kms-grant-allow-only-one-key-temporary); attach AdministratorAccess to the developer roles (trap kms-trap-iam-policy-alone-opens-key, misconception that an admin policy overrides the key policy). Two plausible finalists: the account principal statement and a grant.

tasks.title: Disable a KMS key and watch decryption stop
tasks.kills: "You can delete a KMS key at once, and a disabled key is gone."
tasks.plan: In AWS CloudShell: create a symmetric customer managed key tagged book=saa and task=kms-t01 (capture KeyId); encrypt a short text with it (capture the ciphertext); break it: predict, disable the key, decrypt and observe the failure, explain with a disabled key works in no cryptographic operation [until you re-enable it] (kms-disabled-key-no-crypto-until-reenabled); fix: enable the key and decrypt again; then schedule deletion with --pending-window-in-days 7 and read the deletion date from describe-key, explained with [7 – 30 days] (kms-deletion-waiting-period-7-to-30-days). Cleanup: schedule-key-deletion (SPEC cleanup_pairs create-key). Cost line: a key costs [$1/month] prorated hourly (kms-price-key-storage-per-month), a key scheduled for deletion is not charged (kms-pricing-no-charge-scheduled-deletion), and the few requests are inside the free tier (kms-free-tier-20000-requests). Read-only alternative: list-aliases and describe-key on an existing AWS managed key. Commands must come from an official CLI page in the corpus; check the --plaintext blob format of the pinned CLI.
open_issues: fr-0030: whether the Resource Groups Tagging API lists KMS keys; a key stays in PendingDeletion for at least 7 days, so a tag-filter verify returns the key after cleanup (orchestrator decision, see notes_for_orchestrator)
the KMS tag syntax (TagKey=book,TagValue=saa) matches no entry of tasks.tag_patterns (T106)

tasks.title: Turn on automatic rotation and read the rotation status
tasks.kills: "Rotation gives the key a new key ID, so applications must change."
tasks.plan: In AWS CloudShell: create a symmetric customer managed key tagged book=saa and task=kms-t02; read get-key-rotation-status (rotation is off: kms-rotation-disabled-by-default-cmk); enable-key-rotation with --rotation-period-in-days 90 (the lowest value of [between 90 and 2560 days], kms-rotation-period-range-90-2560-days); read the status again and the unchanged KeyId and Arn in describe-key (kms-rotation-same-logical-key-transparent). No rotation happens inside the task, so no rotation fee (kms-price-rotation-capped-at-second). Cleanup: schedule-key-deletion with a 7-day window. Same open issues as kms-t01.

speak.prompt: If an engineer has full S3 permissions, can that engineer still read the bank's recordings?
speak.plan: Answer: not without kms:Decrypt on the bank's key. How: S3 permission opens the bucket; the object's data key is encrypted under the bank's KMS key; the key policy decides who can decrypt. Watch: a key administrator can change the key policy, so watch key policy changes in CloudTrail. You: 'Which roles must read the bank's recordings today?' must_not_say: 'An S3 administrator can read everything in the bucket' (correction from kms-s3-sse-kms-put-get-permissions); 'Encryption alone stops our engineers' (correction: the key policy does, kms-no-principal-has-access-unless-allowed). Follow-ups: 'What if the engineer is a key administrator?' (kms-key-administrators-cannot-use-key); 'How do we prove who read the files?' (kms-cloudtrail-logs-all-calls).

speak.persona: a startup founder in office hours
speak.prompt: What is the difference between AWS KMS and CloudHSM, and when would we need CloudHSM?
speak.plan: First sentence starts 'Both' (J3): both keep keys in HSMs validated at FIPS 140-3 Level 3 (spoken form 'FIPS one-forty-three, Level three' from the fact card). The difference: AWS runs KMS for you; with CloudHSM you get single-tenant HSMs and you run the cluster, users and backups. Watch: AWS services use CloudHSM keys only through a KMS custom key store. You: 'Does a customer contract ask for single-tenant hardware or for PKCS #11?' must_not_say: 'KMS is only FIPS Level 2' (correction kms-hsm-fips-140-3-level-3); 'AWS can recover CloudHSM keys' (correction cloudhsm-aws-cannot-recover-keys).

cards.front: In AWS KMS, you must control who uses a key and audit each use, with LEAST operational overhead. Which key?
cards.back: A customer managed key with its own key policy.

cards.front: In AWS KMS, can an IAM policy allow use of a key whose key policy does not allow IAM policies?
In AWS KMS, the waiting period before a key is deleted is {{c1::7 – 30 days}}.
AWS KMS or AWS CloudHSM: which gives you a single-tenant HSM cluster in your VPC?
In AWS KMS, the Encrypt operation takes plaintext of up to {{c1::4 KB}}.
In AWS KMS, automatic rotation without a set period rotates every {{c1::365 days}}.
In AWS KMS, a custom automatic rotation period is {{c1::between 90 and 2560 days}}.
In AWS CloudHSM, automatic high availability needs {{c1::at least two HSMs}} in two Availability Zones.
In AWS KMS, can you convert an existing single-Region key into a multi-Region key?
In Amazon RDS, can you share a snapshot encrypted with the AWS managed key?
In AWS KMS, disable a key or delete it: which one can you undo later?
cards.back: Disable; a deleted key cannot be recovered.

cards.front: In AWS KMS, a recovery Region must decrypt data during an outage without a cross-Region call. Which key?
cards.back: A multi-Region key with a replica in the recovery Region.

diagrams.title: Envelope encryption with AWS KMS
diagrams.claim: The KMS key stays in AWS KMS, and only a data key reaches the application.
diagrams.alt: Three actors: an application, AWS KMS and a data store. The application gets a data key from AWS KMS, stores encrypted data with the encrypted key, and later asks AWS KMS to decrypt the key.
messages: kms -> app, label 'Two key copies', dashed
app -> store, label 'Encrypted data and key'
say: The application asks AWS KMS for a data key under a KMS key.
AWS KMS returns the data key in plaintext and encrypted under the KMS key.
The application encrypts the data and stores the encrypted data key with it.
To read, the application sends the encrypted data key to AWS KMS and gets the plaintext key back.
